turns.summary: Designed a ride-hailing backend in Jakarta using SAE for eight microservices, adhering to data residency and no-Kubernetes constraints. The architecture includes Cloud-Native API Gateway, RDS, Tair, SLS, and RocketMQ with dedicated trip event flows. To address the request for real-time analytics, Flink was added to process events from RocketMQ, feeding into Hologres for storage and DataV for visualization. This expands the stack with three new products (Flink, Hologres, DataV) while maintaining existing messaging structures. All requirements are now met with these incremental changes to enable live dashboard capabilities alongside core transactional services.

turns.summary: The user requested real-time trip analytics dashboards. The assistant added Flink to process trip events from RocketMQ, Hologres (in zones A and B) as the analytics store, and Quick BI for visualization. These components complement the existing Jakarta-region architecture using SAE, Cloud-Native API Gateway, RDS, Tair, RocketMQ, SLS, ARMS, ESA, and DNS. Open questions regarding scaling policies, security configurations, and disaster recovery strategies remain unresolved. No other architectural changes were made; the new data flow connects RocketMQ to Flink, then to Hologres, and finally to Quick BI dashboards.
